notes.title: Deep Dive - The Transformer
notes.scope: The complete decoder-only transformer as the canonical modern LLM architecture, tracing one token from embedding through N blocks (attention + FFN with residuals and norms) to unembedding logits. IN: the full data path, tensor shapes, parameter budget, where compute goes. OUT: attention math internals (link Concept - Attention Mechanism), positional-encoding details (own notes), kernel-level execution (link Deep Dive - FlashAttention).
key_points: Full forward path: token IDs -> embedding lookup (d_model) + positional info -> N identical blocks -> final norm -> unembedding (often weight-tied to embedding) -> logits over vocab; softmax + cross-entropy target
Modern block is pre-norm residual form: x = x + Attn(Norm(x)); x = x + FFN(Norm(x)); contrast with Vaswani 2017 post-norm ordering and why the swap happened
Tensor shapes through the stack: [batch, seq, d_model]; attention reshapes to [batch, heads, seq, d_head] with d_head = d_model/n_heads (commonly 64-128); merge and out-project back to d_model
Parameter budget per block ~12*d_model^2 (4*d^2 for QKVO attention + 8*d^2 for a 4x FFN) plus norms; embedding = vocab*d_model; worked example for GPT-3 175B (n_layers 96, d_model 12288)
Causal masking makes it autoregressive; training uses teacher forcing with next-token cross-entropy computed in parallel across all positions (the key efficiency over RNNs)
Weight tying of input embedding and output unembedding (Press and Wolf 2017); the logit = hidden @ unembedding computation and its vocab-scaled FLOP cost
Where compute goes: attention is O(N^2 * d) and FFN is O(N * d^2); FFN dominates FLOPs at typical sequence lengths, attention dominates memory at long context
Mermaid diagram of one block and the full stack required; call out that everything reads and writes the shared residual stream
links: Concept - Feed-Forward Networks and GLU Variants

notes.title: Concept - Attention Mechanism
notes.scope: Scaled dot-product attention as the sequence-mixing operation at the heart of the transformer. IN: Q/K/V projections, softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V, causal masking, and why the scaling factor exists. OUT: multi-head splitting and head-sharing variants (link Concept - Multi-Head Attention Variants), positional encoding (own note), the fused kernel (link Deep Dive - FlashAttention).
key_points: Q=xW_Q, K=xW_K, V=xW_V; scores S=QK^T; weights A=softmax(S/sqrt(d_k)); output=AV; attention is content-based soft dictionary lookup (queries retrieve values by key similarity)
The 1/sqrt(d_k) scaling: without it dot products have variance proportional to d_k, pushing softmax into a saturated low-entropy regime with vanishing gradients (Vaswani et al. 2017 section 3.2.1)
Causal mask: set S_ij = -inf for j>i before softmax so position i attends only to <=i; this is what enables parallel training against shifted next-token targets
Softmax must be computed in fp32 even in bf16 models; max-subtraction for numerical stability; this is the exact structure FlashAttention fuses to avoid materializing the N-by-N score matrix in HBM
Complexity: O(N^2 * d) time and O(N^2) score memory, the motivation for sparse attention, sliding windows, and linear-attention alternatives
Attention is permutation-equivariant without positional information (dog bites man == man bites dog), which is exactly why positional encoding is mandatory
Failure modes: attention entropy collapse (all mass on one token), rank collapse in deep stacks, and the massive-activation / attention-sink phenomenon on the first token
links: Concept - Multi-Head Attention Variants (MHA MQA GQA MLA)
Concept - Matrix Multiplication as the Atom of Deep Learning

notes.title: Concept - Multi-Head Attention Variants (MHA MQA GQA MLA)
notes.scope: The family of attention head-sharing schemes and the KV-cache-vs-quality tradeoff that drives them. IN: MHA, MQA, GQA, MLA mechanisms and their per-token cache sizes. OUT: attention math basics (link Concept - Attention Mechanism), KV-cache serving and paging (link Concept - KV Cache), the fused kernel (link Deep Dive - FlashAttention).
key_points: MHA: h independent (Q,K,V) heads of width d_head; KV cache = 2 * n_layers * h * d_head * seq_len elements per sequence, the dominant long-context memory term
MQA (Shazeer 2019, one-author paper): a single shared K,V head across all Q heads; cache shrinks by factor h; small quality hit, much faster memory-bound decode
GQA (Ainslie et al. 2023): g KV groups with 1<g<h interpolating MHA<->MQA; LLaMA-2 70B uses 8 KV heads for 64 query heads; the standard modern default

MLA (DeepSeek-V2 2024): low-rank joint compression of K and V into a shared latent (e.g. 512-d) cached instead of full K,V, up-projected per head at compute time; ~1/4 of GQA cache while matching or beating MHA quality

The decoupled-RoPE subtlety in MLA: RoPE cannot be absorbed into the low-rank projection because it is position-dependent, so a small set of RoPE-carrying dims (e.g. 64) is kept separate, the crux practitioners miss
KV cache comparison table across variants; why this matters: decode is memory-bandwidth-bound and KV cache dominates memory at long context and high batch (link Roofline)
Failure modes: MQA training instability requiring uptraining from an MHA checkpoint; GQA group-count as a tuning knob; porting bugs from repeat vs repeat_interleave of KV heads

notes.title: Concept - Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE)
notes.scope: RoPE as the dominant relative positional scheme in modern LLMs. IN: the rotation mechanism, frequency bands, why it encodes relative position, the base theta knob. OUT: context-length-extension methods (link Concept - Context Length Extension), extrapolation folklore and YaRN edge behavior (link 18 esoterica), the broader positional taxonomy (link Concept - Positional Encoding).
key_points: Applies a position-dependent rotation to Q and K in 2D subspaces: token at position m is rotated by m*theta_i in subspace i, with theta_i = base^(-2i/d) and base=10000 by default (Su et al. 2021, RoFormer)
Relative property: <R_m q, R_n k> depends only on (m-n), so the attention dot product becomes a function of relative position with no learned relative-bias table and no added parameters
rotate_half implementation trick; RoPE is applied to Q and K only (never V), after the head reshape, on the d_head dimension

Frequency spectrum: low-index dims rotate fast (local, high-frequency), high-index dims rotate slowly (long-range); the wavelength of the slowest dim versus context length governs extrapolation behavior
The base theta is a folklore-laden knob: LLaMA-3 raised base to 500000 to support longer context; higher base = longer wavelengths = better long-range (link 18 for the extrapolation folklore)
Why RoPE beat learned and sinusoidal absolute encodings: relative, parameter-free, composes with linear attention, and its attention weights decay with distance

Failure modes: naive extrapolation beyond trained length collapses (perplexity explodes) motivating PI/NTK/YaRN; interleaved-vs-half-split ordering mismatch silently breaks weight porting (link Gotchas)
links: Concept - Floating Point for Deep Learning

notes.title: Concept - Mixture of Experts Architecture
notes.scope: The sparse MoE layer that replaces a dense FFN with many experts plus a router, activating only a few experts per token. IN: routing/gating, top-k, experts, shared experts, capacity, and the parameter-vs-compute decoupling. OUT: load-balancing training dynamics and aux-loss engineering (link 04), expert-parallel comms (link 04/08), MoE serving (link 07).
key_points: Replace the FFN sublayer with N expert FFNs + a router; router = linear layer -> logits -> softmax -> top-k gate; output = sum over selected experts of gate_i * Expert_i(x)
Decouples total parameters from active parameters/FLOPs: Mixtral 8x7B is 47B total but ~13B active (top-2 of 8); DeepSeek-V3 is 671B total / 37B active
Top-1 routing (Switch Transformer, Fedus et al. 2021) vs top-2 (GShard, Mixtral); fine-grained many-small-experts plus always-on shared experts (DeepSeekMoE 2024) for better specialization
Expert capacity and capacity factor: each expert processes at most capacity tokens per batch; overflow tokens are dropped (pass through the residual), the token-dropping failure mode
The load-balancing problem: without balancing, routing collapses to a few experts; fixed either by an auxiliary load-balance loss (link 04) or an aux-loss-free routing bias (DeepSeek-V3)
Why MoE: more capacity at fixed active FLOPs; but memory-heavy (all experts resident), comms-heavy (all-to-all dispatch), and batch-dependent at inference
Failure modes: routing collapse, expert under-training, capacity overflow, and train/inference batch mismatch changing which tokens co-occur and thus which get dropped
links: Concept - Feed-Forward Networks and GLU Variants
Concept - Cost Engineering for LLM Applications

notes.title: Concept - State Space Models and Mamba
notes.scope: Structured SSMs as a sub-quadratic sequence-mixing alternative to attention, culminating in Mamba's selective SSM. IN: the linear recurrence, S4/HiPPO, Mamba's input-dependent selection, hardware-aware parallel scan, Mamba-2/SSD. OUT: hybrid designs (link Concept - Hybrid SSM-Attention Architectures), the linear-attention connection (link Concept - Linear Attention), ring/context-parallel extreme context (link 18).
key_points: Continuous SSM h'(t)=Ah+Bu, y=Ch discretized to a linear recurrence h_t = A_bar h_{t-1} + B_bar u_t, y_t = C h_t; runs as an O(N) recurrence or an O(N log N) long convolution
S4 (Gu et al. 2021): HiPPO-initialized structured A gives principled long-range memory; diagonal-plus-low-rank parameterization makes it tractable

Mamba (Gu and Dao 2023): selective SSM where B, C, and the step Delta are input-dependent, breaking the LTI convolution but enabling content-based reasoning; hardware-aware parallel scan keeps state in SRAM
Complexity win: O(N) time and O(1) state per step at inference (constant, KV-free memory) versus attention's linearly growing KV cache, a decisive long-context advantage
Mamba-2 (Dao and Gu 2024): State Space Duality (SSD) shows SSMs are a form of linear attention, giving a matmul-friendly formulation and much larger states
Core weakness: a fixed-size state cannot do exact recall/copying like attention; Mamba underperforms on associative-recall and in-context retrieval, the reason hybrids exist
Real systems: Mamba, Jamba (52B MoE hybrid), Codestral Mamba, Falcon-Mamba, the Griffin/RecurrentGemma lineage
links: Concept - Recurrent Networks and the LSTM

notes.title: Concept - Positional Encoding
notes.scope: The general problem of injecting order into a permutation-equivariant attention stack and the family of solutions. IN: why position is needed, absolute (sinusoidal/learned), relative (Shaw/T5 bias), ALiBi, NoPE, and pointers to RoPE. OUT: RoPE internals (link Concept - Rotary Position Embeddings), context extension (link Concept - Context Length Extension), extrapolation folklore (link 18).
key_points: Self-attention is permutation-equivariant, so without position info word order is invisible; position must be injected somewhere in the stack
Absolute sinusoidal (Vaswani 2017): fixed sin/cos of position at geometric frequencies added to embeddings; learned absolute (BERT, GPT-2): a learned table hard-capped at max training length
Relative position (Shaw et al. 2018; T5 relative-bias buckets; Transformer-XL): bias attention scores by (i-j), giving better length generalization than absolute
ALiBi (Press et al. 2021): add a linear head-specific slope -m*(i-j) to scores; no embeddings, strong length extrapolation, used in BLOOM and MPT
NoPE: decoder-only causal models can learn position implicitly from the causal mask alone and do surprisingly well at small scale (Kazemnejad et al. 2023)
RoPE (own note) is the dominant modern choice; this note is the map, RoPE is the deep dive
Tradeoff axes: extrapolation past trained length, parameter cost, compute cost, and compatibility with KV cache and linear attention

notes.title: Concept - Feed-Forward Networks and GLU Variants
notes.scope: The position-wise FFN sublayer and the gated-linear-unit variants that replaced the vanilla two-layer MLP. IN: FFN structure, expansion ratio, GELU/SwiGLU/GEGLU, the 8/3 parameter-matching rescale, FFN-as-memory view. OUT: activation-function fundamentals (link 02), MoE sparsification (link Concept - Mixture of Experts Architecture), why-4x folklore (link 18).
key_points: Vanilla FFN: y = W_2 * act(W_1 * x); acts position-wise; hidden dim d_ff = 4*d_model conventionally; holds roughly two-thirds of a block's parameters
Activation lineage: ReLU (original) -> GELU (BERT/GPT, smooth) -> SiLU/Swish, chosen for smoother gradients
GLU variants (Shazeer 2020, 'GLU Variants Improve Transformer'): FFN gains a gate, SwiGLU = (Swish(xW) elementwise-mul xV) W_2; GEGLU and ReGLU analogous; consistent perplexity wins
Parameter matching: GLU adds a third matrix, so d_ff is scaled by ~2/3 (LLaMA uses d_ff ~= (8/3)*d_model rounded to a hardware-friendly multiple) to hold params/FLOPs comparable to a vanilla 4x FFN
Real usage: SwiGLU in LLaMA, PaLM, Mistral; GeGLU in Gemma; bias terms are usually dropped in modern FFNs
FFN as key-value memory (Geva et al. 2021): the first matrix acts as keys detecting input patterns, the second as values writing to the residual stream, a bridge to interpretability
Design notes: FFN dominates FLOPs and params so it is exactly what MoE sparsifies; activation choice interacts with fp8 dynamic range and outlier features
links: Concept - Matrix Multiplication as the Atom of Deep Learning

notes.title: Concept - Normalization Placement (Pre-Norm, Post-Norm, DeepNorm)
notes.scope: Where normalization goes relative to the residual connection and why that decides training stability at depth. IN: post-norm vs pre-norm, DeepNorm, sandwich norm, output/QK-norm placement, the residual-growth mechanism. OUT: the norm-layer math itself (link Concept - RMSNorm and LayerNorm), general vanishing-gradient theory (link 02).
key_points: Post-norm (Vaswani 2017): x = Norm(x + Sublayer(x)); strong but unstable when deep, needs careful LR warmup because gradients through the residual pass through the norm

Pre-norm (GPT-2 onward): x = x + Sublayer(Norm(x)); clean gradient highway through the residual, trains stably at depth, but causes growing residual-stream magnitude and representation collapse in very deep nets (Liu et al. 2020)
DeepNorm (Wang et al. 2022): post-norm with residual up-scaling alpha and down-scaled init beta, enabling stable 1000-layer transformers
Sandwich norm (norm before and after the sublayer, revived by Gemma 2); QK-norm and final-logit norm as auxiliary stabilizers (link Attention Logit Stabilization)
The residual-growth mechanism: pre-norm makes each layer an additive contribution on an ever-growing stream, so late layers see relatively smaller normalized updates
Warmup interacts with placement: post-norm demands longer warmup; loss-spike pathology at scale ties directly to placement and residual scaling (link 04 training stability)
Real convergence: nearly all modern LLMs are pre-norm + RMSNorm, but Gemma 2 revived hybrid sandwich norm for stability at scale, showing the choice is not settled
links: Concept - Attention Logit Stabilization (QK-Norm and Soft-Capping)
Deep Dive - Anatomy of a Pretraining Run
Lore - The Standardization of the Transformer Block

notes.title: Concept - The Residual Stream
notes.scope: The transformer's additive skip-connection bus that every sublayer reads from and writes to, and why it is the right mental model for the architecture. IN: additive residuals, the linear communication view, magnitude growth with depth, weight tying to un/embedding. OUT: interpretability techniques built on it (superposition, SAEs, logit lens link 14), general ResNet history (link Concept - Convolutional Neural Networks).
key_points: Each block does x <- x + f(x); the stream is a running sum, so sublayers communicate by writing linear features that later layers read (Elhage et al. 2021, 'A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits')
Linearity of the residual path means gradients flow undamped to early layers, the reason very deep transformers train at all (contrast with pre/post-norm placement)
Attention moves information between positions; FFN processes within a position; both are increments to the same d_model-wide bus
Magnitude grows with depth as each layer adds; LayerNorm/RMSNorm re-scale reads; late-layer massive activations and attention sinks are residual-stream phenomena (link 18)
Un/embedding weight tying plus the logit lens: reading the stream through the unembedding at any layer exposes a running best-guess token distribution
Bottleneck: d_model channels shared by all features forces superposition (link 14); the stream is a scarce communication resource, not a free-form scratchpad
Practical consequence: adding/removing layers, residual scaling, and where you insert a new module all perturb this shared bus, so architecture edits are rarely local

notes.title: Concept - Encoder-Decoder and Decoder-Only Architectures
notes.scope: The taxonomy of transformer configurations by attention masking and its downstream consequences. IN: encoder-only (BERT), decoder-only (GPT), encoder-decoder (T5), cross-attention, PrefixLM, and why decoder-only dominates LLMs. OUT: pretraining objectives / MLM-vs-CLM training details (link 04), specific model breakdowns (own notes).
key_points: Encoder-only (BERT, Devlin 2018): full bidirectional attention, masked-language-model objective, produces representations for classification/retrieval, cannot generate autoregressively
Decoder-only (GPT lineage): causal mask, next-token objective, unifies understanding and generation, and unlocks in-context learning
Encoder-decoder (original Transformer, T5): a bidirectional encoder plus a causal decoder joined by cross-attention; strong for seq2seq tasks like translation and summarization
Cross-attention mechanism: Q comes from the decoder, K/V from the encoder output; this is the one architectural piece not present in decoder-only models
PrefixLM / non-causal prefix (UL2, GLM): the prompt is attended bidirectionally while the target is generated causally, a middle ground
Why decoder-only won for LLMs: a single objective scales cleanly, no encoder/decoder parameter split, in-context learning, and KV-cache-friendly generation (Wang et al. 2022 architecture comparison)
Where encoders persist: embedding models/retrievers (link 11) and rerankers still use bidirectional encoders because they need whole-sequence representations, not generation
links: Lore - The Standardization of the Transformer Block

notes.title: Concept - Context Length Extension
notes.scope: Post-hoc architectural methods to run a RoPE model beyond its trained context length. IN: Position Interpolation, NTK-aware scaling, YaRN, ABF/base-change, dynamic scaling, and the RoPE-frequency mechanism each uses. OUT: RoPE internals (link Concept - Rotary Position Embeddings), extrapolation folklore/edge behavior (link 18), long-context serving/KV memory (link 07), context-rot quality (link 09).
key_points: The problem: a RoPE model trained to length L degrades sharply past L because high-frequency dims see rotation phases never observed in training; naive extrapolation makes perplexity explode
Position Interpolation (Chen et al. 2023): linearly downscale position indices by L/L' so all positions fall in the trained range; needs a brief fine-tune; loses high-frequency resolution

NTK-aware scaling: change the RoPE base theta so high frequencies are barely touched and low frequencies stretched, extending without fine-tuning; Dynamic NTK adjusts the scale to the current sequence length
YaRN (Peng et al. 2023): per-frequency interpolation (NTK-by-parts) plus an attention-temperature (1/sqrt(t)) correction; reaches 128k with minimal fine-tuning
ABF / base change (Xiong et al. 2023, Effective Long-Context Scaling): simply raise base theta (e.g. 10k -> 500k) then fine-tune, the LLaMA-3 approach
Evaluation caveat: passkey/needle tests pass long before real long-context reasoning does, so effective context is far shorter than advertised context (link Context Rot)
Interactions: extension changes attention entropy/temperature, and KV cache plus serving cost scale with the new advertised length (link 07)
links: Deep Dive - Anatomy of a Pretraining Run

notes.title: Concept - Sparse and Sliding-Window Attention
notes.scope: Architectural attention-sparsity patterns that cut the O(N^2) cost by restricting which positions attend to which. IN: sliding-window/local, dilated, global+local (Longformer/BigBird), Sparse Transformer strided patterns, Mistral SWA. OUT: the exact FlashAttention kernel (link 08), ring attention / extreme context (link 18), MoE sparsity (link Concept - Mixture of Experts Architecture).
key_points: Sliding-window attention (Mistral 7B, window 4096): each token attends to the previous w tokens; stacking L layers gives an effective receptive field ~L*w while capping per-token cost at O(w)
Longformer (Beltagy et al. 2020): sliding window plus task-specific global tokens (e.g. [CLS]); BigBird (Zaheer et al. 2020): window + random + global with a universal-approximation argument
Sparse Transformer (Child et al. 2019): strided/fixed factorized patterns reduce N^2 to N*sqrt(N)
Local-vs-global tradeoff: pure local loses long-range exact recall, which is exactly why global layers are interleaved (link Pattern - Interleaving Global and Local Attention)
KV-cache benefit: a sliding window bounds the cache to w tokens per layer, a large serving-memory win, at the cost of exact long-range recall (link 07)
Streaming variants keep the first-k tokens plus the window (StreamingLLM) to preserve stability, tying into the attention-sink phenomenon (link 18)
Failure mode: information beyond the window can only propagate multi-hop through depth, degrading long-range exact-match and copy tasks
links: Pattern - Interleaving Global and Local Attention

notes.title: Concept - Convolutional Neural Networks
notes.scope: The convolutional architecture family as the pre-transformer workhorse and still-relevant lineage. IN: convolution mechanics, receptive field, weight sharing/equivariance, ResNet skip connections, the key architectures. OUT: Vision Transformers (link Concept - Vision Transformers), diffusion U-Nets (link 15), general backprop (link Concept - Backpropagation).
key_points: Convolution: a learned kernel slides over the input computing local dot products; weight sharing gives translation equivariance and far fewer parameters than a dense layer
Receptive field grows with depth, stride, and dilation; a feature hierarchy emerges (edges -> textures -> objects); pooling downsamples spatially
Key lineage: LeNet-5 (1998) -> AlexNet (2012, the ImageNet/GPU moment) -> VGG (stacks of 3x3) -> ResNet (He et al. 2015, skip connections enabling 100+ layers) -> EfficientNet (compound scaling)
Residual/skip-connection origin: ResNet solved the degradation and vanishing-gradient problems in deep nets, the idea the transformer residual stream directly inherits
Efficiency tricks: 1x1 convs for channel mixing, depthwise-separable convs (MobileNet), dilated convs for larger receptive field without extra parameters
Where CNNs still win: small-data vision, edge/latency-constrained deployment, and a strong spatial inductive bias versus the data-hungry ViT (link 15)
Conceptual bridge: a convolution is like attention with a fixed local kernel; ViT replaced the fixed inductive bias with learned global attention
links: Concept - Recurrent Networks and the LSTM

notes.title: Concept - Recurrent Networks and the LSTM
notes.scope: The RNN lineage that preceded transformers, why gating solved vanishing gradients, and why parallelism killed RNNs for LLMs. IN: vanilla RNN, BPTT, LSTM/GRU gating, seq2seq and the attention origin. OUT: the modern SSM revival (link Concept - State Space Models and Mamba), linear attention (link Concept - Linear Attention), backprop mechanics (link Concept - Backpropagation).
key_points: Vanilla RNN: h_t = tanh(W_h h_{t-1} + W_x x_t); trained by backprop-through-time; suffers vanishing/exploding gradients over long sequences (Bengio et al. 1994)
LSTM (Hochreiter and Schmidhuber 1997): a cell state plus input/forget/output gates create an additive gradient path (the forget gate acts like a residual highway) enabling long-range memory
GRU (Cho et al. 2014): reset and update gates, fewer parameters, similar performance in practice
Seq2seq (Sutskever et al. 2014) plus Bahdanau attention (2014): attention was invented to fix the RNN encoder's fixed-vector bottleneck, the seed that grew into the transformer
Why RNNs lost: inherently sequential over time, so no within-sequence parallelism and poor GPU utilization; transformers process all positions in parallel
The comeback context: SSMs/Mamba and linear attention are effectively RNNs done right, constant-state inference with parallelizable training (link SSM note)
Era tribal knowledge that still matters: gradient clipping, truncated BPTT, and orthogonal/identity initialization for recurrent weight matrices
links: Concept - State Space Models and Mamba

notes.title: Concept - Linear Attention
notes.scope: Attention reformulated to O(N) by removing the softmax and exploiting associativity, and its equivalence to fast-weight RNNs. IN: kernel feature maps, the (K^T V) associativity trick, the recurrent form, Performer/linear-transformer lineage, modern gated variants. OUT: full softmax attention (link Concept - Attention Mechanism), SSMs (link Concept - State Space Models and Mamba), the exact kernels (link 08).
key_points: Softmax attention is O(N^2) because softmax(QK^T) cannot be factored; replacing exp(q.k) with phi(q).phi(k) for a feature map phi lets you compute phi(Q)(phi(K)^T V), reordering to O(N * d^2)
Recurrent view (Katharopoulos et al. 2020): linear attention is an RNN with a matrix-valued hidden state S_t = S_{t-1} + phi(k_t) v_t^T, giving constant-memory inference like SSMs
Performer (Choromanski et al. 2020): random-feature (FAVOR+) approximation of the softmax kernel; other kernels use elu+1 or ReLU feature maps
The catch: linear attention underperforms softmax on recall and associative tasks because it loses the spiky softmax that performs sharp exact lookup
Modern revival: gated linear attention (GLA), RetNet's exponential decay, DeltaNet, and the SSM-linear-attention duality (Mamba-2 SSD), all fast-weight RNNs with different gating/decay rules
Practical role: high throughput and long-context inference where exact recall is not critical; usually hybridized with a few full-attention layers (link Hybrid note)
Failure modes: numerical issues from unbounded feature maps and unbounded state growth (forgetting) without a decay/gating term
links: Concept - State Space Models and Mamba
Concept - Recurrent Networks and the LSTM

notes.title: Concept - Hybrid SSM-Attention Architectures
notes.scope: Models that interleave attention and SSM/linear-recurrent layers to combine exact recall with cheap long-context inference. IN: why hybrids, layer ratios, real systems (Jamba/Griffin/Zamba/Nemotron-H), where full-attention layers go. OUT: SSM internals (link Concept - State Space Models and Mamba), linear attention (link Concept - Linear Attention), MoE (link Concept - Mixture of Experts Architecture).
key_points: Motivation: pure SSM/linear models fail exact copy and associative recall, and a small fraction of full-attention layers restores it cheaply (Jelassi et al. 2024, 'attention is needed for recall')
Jamba (AI21 2024): interleaves Mamba, attention, and MoE layers at roughly 1 attention per 7 Mamba; 256k context with a small KV footprint that fits a single GPU
Griffin / RecurrentGemma (De et al. 2024): gated linear recurrence (RG-LRU) blocks plus local attention, matching transformer quality with faster inference
Design knobs: attention-to-recurrence ratio, placement of attention layers (early vs periodic), full vs sliding-window attention, and whether to add MoE on top
Inference win: most layers carry only a constant-size recurrent state, so the KV cache is dominated by the few attention layers and long-context memory scales far better (link 07)
Data points: Nemotron-H, Zamba2, Falcon-Mamba (2024-2025); an emerging consensus that roughly 5-15% attention layers is enough
Open question (frontier, weakly settled): optimal attention placement and whether hybrids reach frontier quality at the largest scales
links: Concept - State Space Models and Mamba

notes.title: Concept - Multi-Token Prediction
notes.scope: Architecting a model to predict several future tokens per position instead of one, as both a training signal and an inference accelerator. IN: MTP heads, DeepSeek-V3's sequential MTP module, Meta's parallel-head MTP, the self-speculative-decoding payoff. OUT: speculative-decoding serving mechanics (link Concept - Speculative Decoding), standard next-token training (link 04), distillation (link 06).
key_points: Standard LMs predict only token t+1; MTP adds auxiliary objectives/heads predicting t+2, t+3, ... giving a denser gradient signal per position
Meta MTP (Gloeckle et al. 2024): n independent output heads on a shared trunk predict the next n tokens in parallel, improving sample efficiency and providing a free self-speculative draft
DeepSeek-V3 MTP: a sequential MTP module (an extra transformer block) predicts the second-next token while keeping the causal chain intact; used as an auxiliary training loss
Why it helps training: it forces representations that plan ahead and densifies the learning signal, with reported gains concentrated in code and reasoning
Inference payoff: the extra heads are a built-in draft model, enabling speculative decoding without a separate draft model; DeepSeek reports roughly 1.8x decode speedup from acceptance
Design choices: parallel independent heads vs a sequential module, the loss weighting of the extra heads, and whether to keep or discard the heads at inference
Status: promising but not universal, with gains uneven across tasks; actively evolving frontier technique
links: Deep Dive - Anatomy of a Pretraining Run

notes.title: Breakdown - Mixtral 8x7B
notes.scope: Mistral's sparse-MoE model as the canonical, well-documented open MoE. IN: exact config, top-2-of-8 routing, param/active math, the expert-specialization finding, serving implications. OUT: general MoE theory (link Concept - Mixture of Experts Architecture), load-balancing training (link 04), expert-parallel serving (link 07/04).
key_points: Config: 32 layers, d_model 4096, 8 experts per layer, top-2 routing, 47B total params and ~13B active per token; only the FFN sublayers are MoE, attention stays dense
Router: a per-layer linear gate -> softmax over 8 -> top-2 experts, with the two gate weights renormalized before combining expert outputs
Param math: shared attention and embeddings plus 8x the FFN per layer explains why 8x7B is 47B, not 56B; the naming double-counts the shared components
Inheritance from Mistral 7B: GQA (8 KV heads), SwiGLU, pre-norm RMSNorm, and RoPE
Expert-specialization finding: experts do NOT specialize by topic; routing is largely syntactic/positional and fairly uniform across experts (Jiang et al. 2024), a widely misunderstood result
Serving reality: you must hold all 47B in memory though only 13B is active, so it is memory-bound like a big dense model but compute-light like a small one; batching changes the active-expert set
What to steal vs what is dated: the clean top-2 recipe transfers, but it is superseded by fine-grained + shared-expert designs (DeepSeek) that specialize better

notes.title: Breakdown - DeepSeek-V3 Architecture
notes.scope: DeepSeek-V3 as the 2024-25 high-water mark of efficient architecture design: MLA + fine-grained MoE + aux-loss-free balancing + MTP + fp8. IN: each architectural decision and its mechanism. OUT: fp8 training-systems details (link 04/08), RL post-training / R1 (link 06), serving internals (link 07).
key_points: Scale: 671B total / 37B active, 61 layers, trained on 14.8T tokens for ~2.8M H800 GPU-hours, the cost-efficiency headline that shocked the field
MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention): compresses K,V to a ~512-d latent cached per token with decoupled RoPE dims (64) carried separately, giving ~1/4 the KV cache of GQA at higher quality
DeepSeekMoE: 256 fine-grained routed experts (top-8) plus 1 always-on shared expert per layer; fine-grained many-small-experts improve specialization and combinatorial routing capacity

Aux-loss-free load balancing (Wang et al. 2024): a per-expert bias is added to routing logits and nudged up/down by observed load instead of a gradient auxiliary loss, avoiding the aux-loss-vs-quality tradeoff, a decision worth stealing
Multi-Token Prediction module: a sequential extra block predicting the second-next token densifies training signal and doubles as a speculative draft (~1.8x decode)
fp8 mixed precision with fine-grained (tile/block) quantization plus DualPipe scheduling (link 04/08) is how they hit the cost number
What to steal: MLA for KV-bound serving, bias-based balancing, MTP-as-draft; what is specialized: the fp8/comms co-design assumes their exact H800 cluster topology
links: Concept - Multi-Head Attention Variants (MHA MQA GQA MLA)

notes.title: Reference - Transformer Architecture Cheat Sheet
notes.scope: Fast lookup for transformer dimensions, parameter-count and FLOP formulas, and side-by-side configs of real models. IN: param/FLOP formulas, shape conventions, a model-config comparison table. OUT: memory-during-training math (link Reference - Memory Math for Transformers), attention KV-cache serving math (link 07).
key_points: Parameter formulas per block: attention ~4*d_model^2 (QKVO; less with GQA/MLA), FFN 2*d_ff*d_model (3*d_ff*d_model with a GLU gate) plus norms; embedding = vocab*d_model
Total-param approximation N ~= 12 * n_layers * d_model^2 for a dense pre-norm decoder (valid when d_ff=4d and MHA), with correction notes for GQA, GLU, and MoE
FLOPs conventions: forward ~= 2N per token, training ~= 6N per token (Kaplan/Chinchilla), the basis for compute budgeting (link Scaling Laws)
Config comparison table columns: d_model, n_layers, n_heads, n_kv_heads, d_head, d_ff, vocab, activation, norm, positional scheme, context length, total/active params
Rows: GPT-2, GPT-3 175B, LLaMA-2 7B/70B, LLaMA-3, Mistral 7B, Mixtral 8x7B, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen2.5, Gemma 2 (date-stamped as of 2026)
Conventions worth tabulating: head_dim 64/128, d_ff rounding to hardware-friendly multiples, and the vocab-size trend 32k -> 128k -> 256k

notes.title: Decision - Dense vs Mixture-of-Experts
notes.scope: Choosing between a dense model and a sparse MoE at a fixed training or serving budget. IN: the tradeoff axes (quality-per-FLOP, memory, comms, serving batch, fine-tuning) and when each wins. OUT: MoE architecture internals (link Concept - Mixture of Experts Architecture), expert-parallel systems (link 04/08), serving batching (link 07).
key_points: Core tradeoff: MoE buys more parameters (capacity/quality) at roughly constant active FLOPs, but pays in total memory (all experts resident), all-to-all comms, and serving complexity
When MoE wins: training-compute-bound regimes and high-throughput serving where memory is available (Mixtral, DeepSeek, Qwen-MoE data points)
When dense wins: memory-constrained deployment, low or variable batch (single-user latency), simpler fine-tuning and quantization, and edge devices

Serving nuance: MoE needs large batches to keep experts busy; at batch=1 you pay full memory bandwidth for the whole model while getting only small-model compute, often a wash or worse than a same-active dense model
Fine-tuning/quantization friction: MoE routers are brittle to post-training quantization and small-data fine-tunes can wreck load balance (link 12)
Rule of thumb (folklore): a MoE gives roughly the quality of a dense model with sqrt(total * active) parameters; token-choice vs expert-choice routing shifts the calculus
Decision flow: identify the binding budget (train-FLOP vs serve-memory vs latency), the batch profile, and the team's infra maturity for expert parallelism
links: Concept - Cost Engineering for LLM Applications

notes.title: Decision - Choosing a Sequence Mixer
notes.scope: Selecting the token-mixing layer(s) for a new model: full attention, sliding-window, linear attention, SSM, or a hybrid. IN: the recall-vs-cost tradeoff, context-length target, training/inference budget, ecosystem risk. OUT: each mechanism's internals (link respective notes), kernels (link 08).
key_points: Primary axis: exact in-context recall (full attention best) versus long-context inference cost (SSM/linear best, constant state); recall effectively costs memory
Full attention: gold standard for recall/reasoning, O(N^2) training and a linearly growing KV cache at serve time, still the default for frontier quality
Sliding-window: bounded KV cache and cheap, but loses exact long-range recall unless interleaved with global layers
Linear attention / SSM: O(N) training, constant-state inference, weak exact recall, good for streaming, long audio, and genomics
Hybrid (a few full-attention layers plus a recurrent majority): current best long-context/quality tradeoff (Jamba, Griffin); choose the attention ratio and placement
Decision flow: target context length, whether exact retrieval is required, train-vs-inference cost priority, and willingness to leave the well-supported full-attention path
Ecosystem risk (often decisive): full attention has FlashAttention and vLLM/SGLang support; exotic mixers have thin kernel and serving support (link 07/08)
links: Concept - State Space Models and Mamba

notes.title: Gotchas - Implementing Attention
notes.scope: The bugs that produce a model which trains but is subtly wrong, specific to hand-implementing attention and positional encoding. IN: masking, scaling, dtype, reshape, RoPE application, GQA repeat, padding. OUT: MoE-specific gotchas (link Gotchas - Mixture of Experts), kernel numerics (link 08).
key_points: Causal mask off-by-one / wrong triangle: letting a token see itself+future or masking the diagonal; symptom is suspiciously low training loss (label leakage), detect with a causality self-test on shifted targets
Softmax in bf16/fp16: computing softmax in low precision overflows or loses mass; scores must be upcast to fp32 before softmax then cast back (link Floating Point)
Missing or wrong 1/sqrt(d_head) scale (or scaling by d_model instead of d_head): attention entropy collapses and loss plateaus high
Head reshape/transpose bugs: mixing head and feature dims via view vs permute silently scrambles heads while output shape still looks plausible; catch with a per-head identity unit test
RoPE applied to the wrong dims, after an incorrect head split, or to V; interleaved-vs-half ordering and base/theta mismatch versus the reference garble long-context (link RoPE, Playbook)
GQA/MQA repeat_kv: forgetting to expand KV heads to the query-head count, or using repeat vs repeat_interleave, silently mis-groups keys and values
Padding and causal-mask interaction in batched training (attending to pad tokens); left- vs right-padding at inference breaks position indices and RoPE offsets

notes.title: Gotchas - Mixture of Experts
notes.scope: Architecture-level MoE pitfalls that survive into inference and fine-tuning, distinct from at-scale training load-balancing (owned by 04). IN: routing collapse, capacity/dropping, batch dependence, PTQ brittleness, shared-expert bookkeeping, gate precision. OUT: aux-loss training dynamics (link 04), expert-parallel comms bugs (link 04/08).
key_points: Routing collapse / dead experts: a few experts win everything and the rest never train; symptom is a spiky load histogram, detect by logging per-expert token counts (fix via aux-loss or bias, link 04)

Token dropping under a capacity factor < 1.0: overflow tokens skip the expert and pass through the residual, causing silent quality loss and a train/eval mismatch when capacity differs between the two

Batch-size dependence at inference: which tokens share a batch changes expert load and, with capacity limits, changes outputs, producing nondeterminism across batch sizes; drop capacity limits or use large capacity at inference
Post-training quantization brittleness: routers and low-magnitude expert weights are sensitive, and naive GPTQ/AWQ can flip routing decisions (link 07 quantization)
Shared-vs-routed expert bookkeeping: forgetting the always-on shared expert (DeepSeek-style) or double-counting parameters when computing active params
Gate precision and normalization: computing gates in low precision or forgetting to renormalize the top-k gate weights shifts the output scale
Fine-tuning a MoE: small datasets can wreck routing balance, so freezing routers or using a low LR on the gates is common tribal practice (link 12)

notes.title: Snippet - Scaled Dot-Product Attention from Scratch
notes.scope: A minimal, correct, runnable PyTorch implementation of causal multi-head attention. IN: projections, reshape, scaled scores, causal mask, fp32 softmax, output projection, a causality self-test. OUT: RoPE (link Snippet - RoPE Implementation), the KV-cache generation loop (link 07), the fused kernel (link 08).
key_points: ~40-line nn.Module: qkv projection, reshape to [B,H,T,d_head], scores = q @ k.transpose(-2,-1) / sqrt(d_head), causal mask via triu(-inf), softmax(dim=-1), @ v, merge heads, out-projection
Show the causal mask constructed correctly (upper-triangular -inf, diagonal kept) and applied before softmax
Show the explicit fp32 upcast of scores before softmax and the cast back, the numerical-stability decision spelled out
Comment the sqrt(d_head) scale and why (variance control so softmax does not saturate)
Runnable __main__ with a random input, an assertion on output shape, and a causality test proving position t's output is independent of tokens > t
Why-it-is-written-this-way: fp32 softmax, the causality self-test, and the reshape/transpose order that avoids the classic head-scramble bug
Header block states dependencies (torch version) and expected printed output

notes.title: Snippet - RoPE Implementation
notes.scope: A correct, runnable RoPE application showing the frequency computation and the rotate_half trick. IN: inv_freq, position angles, cos/sin caches, applying rotation to Q and K, an empirical relative-position check. OUT: RoPE theory (link Concept - Rotary Position Embeddings), context-extension scaling (link Concept - Context Length Extension).
key_points: Compute inv_freq = 1 / base^(arange(0,d,2)/d); outer product with positions gives angles; build cos and sin tensors
rotate_half(x): split the last dim in half and return cat(-x2, x1); apply q_rot = q*cos + rotate_half(q)*sin, same for k
Show that only Q and K are rotated (never V), applied after the head reshape, on the d_head dimension
Expose base/theta as a parameter and comment where NTK/YaRN scaling would hook in (link Context Length Extension)
Runnable test that empirically verifies the relative-position property: the dot product of rotated q_m and k_n depends only on (m - n)
Why-it-is-written-this-way: the interleaved-vs-half-split convention mismatch (GPT-NeoX vs original RoPE ordering) that silently breaks weight porting, the single most common RoPE bug (link Playbook)
Header block states torch version and the expected printed relative-property check output

notes.title: Snippet - Top-2 MoE Routing Layer
notes.scope: A minimal runnable sparse-MoE FFN layer with top-2 token-choice routing. IN: the gate, top-k selection, renormalization, weighted expert combination, per-expert load logging. OUT: capacity/dropping and load-balance loss (link 04 / Gotchas), expert-parallel dispatch (link 04/08).

notes.title: Checklist - New Architecture Bring-Up
notes.scope: Pre-flight verification before committing compute to train a new or modified transformer architecture. IN: shape/param sanity, init, causality, positional correctness, overfit-a-batch, MoE load, throughput sanity. OUT: full training-run operations (link Deep Dive - Anatomy of a Pretraining Run), the data pipeline (link 05).
key_points: Parameter count matches the analytic formula (12 * n_layers * d^2 plus corrections), catching wrong d_ff, missing GLU rescale, or vocab errors
Overfit a single batch to near-zero loss, proving the model can learn and backprop is wired end to end (link The Training Loop)
Causality test: the output at position t is unchanged when tokens > t are perturbed
Positional correctness: shuffling input positions changes the output (position is actually used) and the RoPE base matches the intended context length
Init sanity: activation and gradient RMS are stable across layers at step 0 (no explosion), confirming correct residual/norm placement (link Normalization Placement)
Softmax and logits computed in fp32; no NaN under bf16 for the first hundred steps (link Mixed Precision)
For MoE: every expert receives tokens and the load histogram is not collapsed; capacity factor set intentionally
Throughput / MFU is in the expected range and the attention-vs-FFN FLOP split matches the cheat-sheet estimate (link Roofline)

notes.title: Playbook - Numerically Matching a Reference Implementation
notes.scope: The procedure to port a model architecture to a new codebase and prove it correct against the reference (HF vs original vs your kernel) by diffing activations. IN: weight-name mapping, layer-by-layer activation diffing, the usual culprits, tolerance budgeting. OUT: kernel-level numerics (link 08), quantization mismatch (link 07).
key_points: Goal/when: you reimplemented or converted a model and logits or generations differ from the reference, and you must confirm correctness before trusting a fine-tune or a serving port

Step: freeze both models in eval mode, force the same dtype (start in fp32/fp64 to remove precision noise), feed identical input, compare final logits against a tolerance (e.g. max-abs-diff < 1e-4 in fp32)
Step: if mismatched, binary-search by hooking and diffing per-layer residual-stream activations to localize the first divergent layer

The usual-culprits list: RoPE ordering (interleaved vs half) and base theta; norm epsilon value and inside-vs-outside the sqrt; attention scale (d_head vs d_model); GQA repeat method; SwiGLU gate/up order and d_ff; logit soft-cap/QK-norm presence; embedding weight-tying; BOS/special-token handling
Step: build a weight-name mapping table; the packed-QKV split order (fused qkv sliced into q,k,v in the wrong order) is a top silent bug
Verification: greedy generations are identical for N tokens and perplexity on a fixed text matches to 3-4 significant figures

When-it-goes-wrong branch table: diverges at layer 0 -> embedding/positional; grows with depth -> norm eps or residual scale; only at long context -> RoPE base; only on certain tokens -> tokenizer/special-token

notes.title: Lore - The Standardization of the Transformer Block
notes.scope: The narrative of how the 2017 Vaswani block converged, component by component, into the 2024 LLaMA-standard decoder block, and the people and papers that drove each swap. IN: the sequence of changes and why each stuck. OUT: each component's mechanism (link its own note), the scaling-law drivers (link 04).
key_points: Original (2017): post-norm LayerNorm, sinusoidal absolute PE, ReLU FFN at 4x, MHA with bias terms, encoder-decoder
The decoder-only turn: GPT/GPT-2 drop the encoder, use learned absolute PE, and adopt pre-norm for stability at depth
Noam Shazeer's outsized fingerprints: MQA (2019), the GLU/SwiGLU variants (2020), and the spread of RMSNorm; much of the modern block traces to a handful of his papers
RoPE (RoFormer 2021) displaces absolute PE while ALiBi competes; RoPE wins largely on ecosystem momentum
LLaMA (2023) crystallizes the consensus: pre-norm RMSNorm, RoPE, SwiGLU (d_ff ~= 8/3 * 4d), no bias terms, and GQA in LLaMA-2, and nearly everyone copies it
The counter-current: Gemma 2 (2024) re-adds ideas thought dead (sandwich/post-norm hybrid, logit soft-capping, local/global interleave), showing the standard is not actually settled
Evidence status: mostly well-sourced from papers and model cards, but the why-each-stuck attribution is partly folklore (ecosystem lock-in, not always proven superiority)
links: Concept - Feed-Forward Networks and GLU Variants

notes.title: Pattern - Interleaving Global and Local Attention
notes.scope: The design pattern of alternating full-context (global) attention layers with cheap local/sliding-window layers to bound KV cost while preserving long-range recall. IN: the interleave structure, ratios, real systems, tradeoffs. OUT: sliding-window mechanics (link Concept - Sparse and Sliding-Window Attention), SSM hybrids (link Concept - Hybrid SSM-Attention Architectures), the FlashAttention kernel (link 08).
key_points: Problem/solution: full attention everywhere is O(N^2)*L while local everywhere loses long-range recall; interleave a minority of global layers among local ones to get both
Structure: Gemma 2/3 alternate local (sliding-window) and global layers at roughly 5:1; GPT-OSS and Cohere Command-R use similar patterns; Character.AI experimented with a single global layer
Why it works: local layers move information within a window cheaply while periodic global layers provide long-range mixing, and effective receptive field compounds through depth
KV-cache payoff: only the global layers keep a full-length KV cache while local layers cap at window w, a large serving-memory reduction (link 07)
Knobs: local-to-global ratio, window size, whether global layers use a different RoPE base/scaling, and periodic-vs-blocked placement
Tradeoffs / when-not: retrieval-heavy workloads may need more global layers, it complicates KV-cache paging (link 07), and kernel support for mixed patterns varies
Known uses: Gemma 2/3, GPT-OSS, Cohere Command, with Longformer's global-token scheme as the ancestor

notes.title: Concept - Attention Logit Stabilization (QK-Norm and Soft-Capping)
notes.scope: The small architectural tricks that keep attention logits and training stable at scale: QK-norm, logit soft-capping, and related clamps. IN: the mechanisms, the instability each prevents, the models that use them, and the FlashAttention incompatibility. OUT: general normalization placement (link Concept - Normalization Placement), loss-spike training dynamics (link 04), the norm-layer math (link 02).
key_points: The problem: attention logits (and final logits) can grow unboundedly during training, saturating softmax and causing loss spikes and divergence at scale, the attention-entropy-collapse pathology (Zhai et al. 2023)

QK-norm: apply LayerNorm/RMSNorm to queries and keys before the dot product so logit magnitude is controlled independent of learned weight norms; used in Gemma 2 and the ViT-22B lineage (Dehghani et al. 2023)
Logit soft-capping (Gemma 2): logits = cap * tanh(logits/cap) applied to attention logits (cap=50) and final logits (cap=30) to bound magnitude smoothly
The serving gotcha: soft-capping is incompatible with the standard FlashAttention kernel and is often disabled at inference, a real source of Gemma-porting quality bugs
z-loss / final-logit regularization (PaLM): penalize log Z to keep the softmax normalizer near 1, a related stabilizer from the training side (link 04 training stability)
Interaction with low precision: bounded logits improve fp8/bf16 stability, and unbounded QK products are a known fp8 hazard (link Mixed Precision)
Why unicorn-tier: rarely explained, buried in model cards, and the exact cap values are folklore; evidence from the Gemma 2 tech report and ViT-22B
links: Deep Dive - Anatomy of a Pretraining Run
